title: Astrid and the Signal
premise: Cyrus Crane, a nonbinary insurance investigator who faked their death seven years ago to escape a corporate massacre, has kept their head down hauling cargo through contested orbits between the Meridian Combine and the Free Belt fleets. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream—a signal from the derelict station where Cyrus's old crew died—investigators from both sides descend, each believing the other is broadcasting a weapon. To keep two armed fleets from open war, Cyrus must resurrect their dead identity and testify to a crime no court will touch, trading their anonymity for justice they once fled. In the end, Cyrus survives as neither ghost nor hero: the lie that held the fleets apart becomes public truth, but the children's dream fades, leaving only what people choose to remember.
about_author: Elodie Villalobos is a former maritime insurance adjuster who turned to science fiction after a decade of investigating 'impossible' losses at sea. She writes from a houseboat in Valparaíso, where she insists the fog improves her plotting.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A routine cargo inspection at Ceres Station reveals tampering disguised as an impossible accident—the kind of fraud Cyrus used to investigate under another name. The beat is wary competence masking old fear; someone out there still knows how Cyrus thinks.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream in Unison
chapters.summary: Colony teacher Mara Okonkwo's POV. Forty children describe the same dream: a corridor of blue light and a voice counting down. Mara reports it and is quietly told to stop asking. Emotional beat: maternal dread meeting institutional stonewalling.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cross-referencing the sabotage with seven-year-old claims files, Cyrus finds their own forged death certificate—and a claim filed last month using their birth name. Beat: the past knocking with paperwork.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Harbor
chapters.summary: Combine liaison Officer Voss's POV. Voss arrives at Ceres convinced the Free Belt is testing a broadcast weapon; her chapters reveal the fleets' fragile armistice. Beat: cold professionalism hiding genuine terror of another war.

chapters.title: What the Signal Says
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She records the children reciting the dream together and recognizes coordinates matching the derelict station Halcyon-9, site of the massacre officially blamed on Belt terrorists. Beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into danger.

chapters.title: A Name I Buried
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The fraudulent claimant turns out to be Dev Raskin, sole surviving crewmate, who faked his own death too and is now baiting whoever buried them both. Beat: fury, relief, and the ache of a friend thought lost.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Courtesy
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss interviews Cyrus about the cargo tampering and lets slip she has a sealed file on the Halcyon incident—one that names a witness who died. Beat: cat-and-mouse where both cats suspect the mouse.

chapters.title: Halcyon-9
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Dev's shared POV, alternating sections. They dock with the derelict and find the black core intact, plus evidence the massacre was ordered by Combine executives to seize Belt mining patents. Beat: grief made physical in frozen corridors.

chapters.title: The Dream Is a Recording
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The signal is a distress beacon on a loop, keyed to juvenile neural implants sold colony-wide—a Combine product. The children aren't haunted; they're addressed. Beat: righteous anger on behalf of the small.

chapters.title: Armistice Terms
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Both fleets mobilize over the signal; Voss is ordered to secure Halcyon-9 and silence witnesses if necessary. Beat: the moment a decent officer realizes she serves the crime.

chapters.title: Insurance Against the Truth
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Dev wants to sell the black core's data to the Belt fleet; Cyrus knows either fleet weaponizing it means war. Beat: the survivor's instinct to run colliding with the investigator's need for the record.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Classroom
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Combine agents raid the school seeking the children's implant logs; Mara hides the drives inside a lesson about tide pools. Beat: quiet courage, ordinary heroism against bureaucratic menace.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Died
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss discovers the 'dead' witness in her file matches Cyrus Crane's face and begins her own private investigation of her employers. Beat: loyalty cracking into doubt.

chapters.title: Dev's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev contacts the Belt fleet anyway and is captured mid-handoff; the Combine tortures him for the core's location. Beat: betrayal of trust, and guilt Cyrus will carry.

chapters.title: Resurrection Papers
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. To save Dev, Cyrus must un-dead themselves legally—filing the true Halcyon claim through the very insurance system that erased them. Beat: terror and grim humor in signing one's own name again.

chapters.title: The Hearing Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. On neutral Ceres, Cyrus testifies before joint arbitrators while Voss corroborates with the sealed file; the Combine moves to declare the hearing invalid. Beat: truth versus procedure, justice outside the law beginning here.

chapters.title: Fleet Shadow
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. A Combine strike team launches to destroy Halcyon-9 and the evidence with it; Voss defects just enough to warn Cyrus. Beat: the cost of conscience, paid in career and country.

chapters.title: Blue Corridor
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Mara's alternating POV. Racing the strike team, they reach the station and broadcast the black core raw to every implant in the colony—the children's dream becomes everyone's memory. Beat: catharsis; the dead finally witnessed.

chapters.title: What Holds Two Fleets Apart
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. With the truth public, both fleets stand down rather than fight over a crime already confessed—but hardliners move on Ceres itself. Beat: victory shadowed by retaliation.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Dev's POV, recovering. Dev chooses exile over testimony's aftermath, telling Cyrus that surviving sometimes means leaving. Beat: bittersweet farewell; not every wound closes.

chapters.title: Verdict Without a Court
chapters.summary: Voss and Cyrus's shared POV. The executives are convicted by public record if not by tribunal; Voss resigns, Cyrus declines reinstatement. Beat: justice achieved imperfectly, identity chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: After the Signal Fades
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, closing. The children stop dreaming; one asks Cyrus if being remembered was worth losing everything. Cyrus answers: staying invisible was never really living. Final beat: quiet dawn over Ceres, a name spoken aloud without flinching.
